_meta.name: Cases demo seed
_meta.note: Entirely fictional demo data. Customers, entities, references and numbers are invented; alert content is adapted from the RegRadar Academy casebook (fictional). Ages are relative to the moment the demo is first loaded.

alerts.title: Six cash deposits in eleven days
alerts.customer: Retail · Ms L. Peeters · customer since 2011 · low risk
alerts.summary: Six cash deposits of between €8,000 and €9,600, all at branch counters, over eleven days. No prior cash activity of any size on this account in fourteen years.
alerts.onFile: No supporting documentation on file. Relationship manager has not been contacted.

alerts.title: Salary account suddenly forwarding funds
alerts.customer: Retail · Mr D. Okonkwo · customer since 2024 · standard risk
alerts.summary: Twelve inbound transfers from unrelated private individuals, each €2,900–€4,600, followed within hours by outbound transfers to three accounts abroad. Balance returns to near zero each time.
alerts.onFile: Customer is 21, opened the account for a student job. No business activity declared. Two inbound senders appear in an internal fraud-victim list.

alerts.title: €180,000 to a notary
alerts.customer: Retail · Mr & Mrs Vandenberghe · customers since 2003 · low risk
alerts.summary: A single transfer of €180,000 to a Belgian notary account, referenced with a property address. Funded by the closure of a savings account held at the same bank since 2009.
alerts.onFile: Savings account shows fourteen years of regular monthly contributions. Mortgage application with this bank was approved two weeks earlier for the same address.

alerts.title: Trade payments routed through three countries
alerts.customer: Corporate · Meridian Trading BVBA · customer since 2019 · high risk
alerts.summary: Four payments for machinery parts, invoiced by a UAE intermediary, with goods shipped directly from Pakistan to Belgium. Invoice values are 40–60% above comparable market pricing.
alerts.onFile: Gulf Machinery FZE was incorporated four months ago. Beneficial owner not established — corporate shareholder in a jurisdiction with no public register. Goods never enter the UAE.

alerts.title: Dormant account wakes up with a round sum
alerts.customer: Retail · Mr S. Haddad · customer since 2016 · standard risk
alerts.summary: A single inbound transfer of €25,000 from a French bank, reference "prêt familial". No subsequent activity. Funds remain in the account.

txs.party: from Crédit Mutuel, ref: prêt familial

alerts.onFile: Sender name matches the customer’s surname. Customer address updated to France in 2021. No adverse media. Funds have not moved.

alerts.title: Three accounts, one pattern
alerts.customer: Retail · Three unrelated customers, same branch · all standard risk
alerts.summary: Three customers with no declared relationship each deposited cash on the same three dates, at the same branch, in amounts between €4,500 and €6,200 — then each transferred the balance to a single fourth account within 48 hours.

facts.Profile: Three individual accounts, no declared connection

alerts.onFile: The receiving account belongs to a company whose director is the brother of customer A. The company is a car dealership.

alerts.title: A 78% name match on a designated person
alerts.customer: Retail · Mr A. Kuznetsov · customer since 2018 · standard risk
alerts.summary: Screening flagged the customer against a designated individual on the EU consolidated list at 78% fuzzy match. The alert relates to a routine €2,300 rent payment.
alerts.onFile: Designated person: Aleksei KUZNETSOV, born 1961, Russian national, resident Moscow. Customer: Anton KUZNETSOV, born 1989, Belgian national, born in Ghent, holds Belgian ID verified at onboarding. Different date of birth, different first name, different nationality.

alerts.title: Inbound from an exchange, onward to a private wallet
alerts.customer: Retail · Ms N. Ferreira · customer since 2022 · standard risk
alerts.summary: Four inbound transfers from a crypto exchange registered in Estonia, then onward transfers to two accounts the customer has not previously used. Chain analytics on the originating addresses shows indirect exposure to a sanctioned mixing service two hops back.
alerts.onFile: Customer declared crypto trading as a side activity at onboarding in 2022. Volumes then were under €5,000 a year. No source-of-wealth documentation on file. Travel-rule originator data absent on three of the four inbound transfers.

alerts.title: A mayor's spouse opens a savings account
alerts.customer: Retail · Mrs C. Lemaire · new customer · PEP-related
alerts.summary: Screening identified the customer as the spouse of a domestic PEP — mayor of a Belgian municipality of 18,000 inhabitants. Initial funding of €35,000 transferred from a joint account held at another Belgian bank.

facts.Profile: Retired teacher, spouse of a municipal mayor

txs.party: joint account, KBC — same customer name

alerts.onFile: Source of funds: proceeds of a property sale, notarial deed provided at onboarding. Senior management approval for the PEP relationship was NOT obtained. Source of wealth documented. No adverse media.

alerts.title: A new merchant's volumes triple in a fortnight
alerts.customer: Corporate · SunGlow Wellness BV · merchant since Jan 2026 · standard risk
alerts.summary: Card acquiring volume rose from €38,000 in February to €310,000 in the first fortnight of March. Chargeback rate 11%. Average ticket €189 against a projected €45. Cardholder geography spread across 31 countries where the merchant declared Benelux-only sales.
alerts.onFile: Merchant declared Benelux-only online sales of supplements at onboarding. Website currently shows a single product page with no stock information. Director appointed three months before onboarding, no prior retail history.

alerts.title: A restaurant's takings rise with its bookings
alerts.customer: Corporate · Trattoria Lucia BVBA · customer since 2014 · standard risk
alerts.summary: Cash deposits of €96,400 across March against a twelve-month average of €58,000. Deposits made weekly, amounts varying between €18,000 and €27,000, all at the same branch.
alerts.onFile: VAT returns filed and consistent with declared turnover. March included Easter weekend and a two-week city food festival. Card takings rose 41% over the same period, proportionate to the cash increase. Same pattern visible in March of the two previous years.
alerts.closeNote: Bookings explained by the restaurant's reservation data; documents on file. Closed without escalation.

alerts.title: Money that goes around in a circle
alerts.customer: Corporate · Novara Consulting BVBA · customer since 2021 · standard risk
alerts.summary: Nine transfers over five weeks. Funds leave the customer to a Luxembourg entity, then to a Cypriot entity, then return to a second Belgian account also held by the customer's director. Each leg carries a consultancy invoice. Net position after five weeks is approximately zero.
alerts.onFile: Corporate registry checks show the director of Novara is also a shareholder of Aurex Sàrl. Kestros Ltd beneficial ownership not established — nominee shareholder. No deliverables, contracts or work product on file for any invoice. Total invoiced exceeds the company's entire prior-year turnover.

alerts.title: New device login, payee changed, large payment out
alerts.customer: Retail · Mr R. Janssens (fictional) · customer since 2017 · low risk
alerts.summary: A login from a device never seen before was followed within ten minutes by a new payee and a payment of EUR 18,500, ten times the customer's largest payment in twelve months.

facts.Expected activity: Salary in, bills and card spend out

alerts.onFile: Customer not yet contacted. Payment pending release.

alerts.title: Customer will not explain a EUR 40,000 incoming transfer
alerts.customer: Retail · Ms K. De Smet (fictional) · customer since 2020 · standard risk
alerts.summary: A branch employee reports that the customer received EUR 40,000 from an unfamiliar company and declined to say what it was for, twice.
alerts.onFile: No documents on file about the sender.

alerts.title: Payments to a counterparty in a high-risk third country
alerts.customer: Corporate · Lindqvist Imports AB (fictional) · customer since 2021 · standard risk
alerts.summary: Two payments totalling EUR 21,000 to a supplier in a jurisdiction on the firm's high-risk list. The supplier is new to this customer.
alerts.onFile: Supplier due diligence not yet performed.

cases.title: Meridian Trading: trade payments via UAE intermediary

timeline.text: Reviewed the four invoices. Intermediary invoices machinery parts but never handles the goods.
Asked the relationship manager for the commercial rationale (internal only; the customer was not contacted).
Relationship manager's explanation contradicts the shipping documents.
Analyst sign-off: recommends reporting to the FIU.

analyst.name: Analyst A
analyst.rationale: The routing, pricing and ownership picture fits a trade-based laundering pattern and the commercial explanation does not hold. Reasonable grounds to suspect are met in my assessment.

narr.legalBasis: AMLR Art. 69(1)(a), or the national law in force until the AMLR applies (10 July 2027)
narr.subjectName: Meridian Trading BVBA (fictional; customer ref CUST-30417)
narr.subjectIds: Customer ref CUST-30417; company number: placeholder only in this demo
narr.relationship: Corporate customer since 2019, import/export, rated high risk
narr.occupation: Import and export of machinery parts, declared turnover EUR 4.1 million
narr.otherParties: Gulf Machinery FZE (UAE intermediary, incorporated four months before the first payment).
narr.activitySummary: Four outbound payments totalling EUR 620,000 were sent to a UAE intermediary for machinery parts that were shipped directly from Pakistan to Belgium and never entered the UAE.
narr.method: The payments were invoiced by Gulf Machinery FZE. Invoice values are 40 to 60 percent above comparable market pricing. The intermediary performs no logistics function and its beneficial owner could not be established: its shareholder is a company in a jurisdiction with no public register.
narr.counterpartyInstitutions: UAE bank of the intermediary (name held on file)
narr.expectedActivity: Trade payments within the EU and to Türkiye; declared annual turnover EUR 4.1 million.
narr.whyText: The destination, the pricing and the routing do not fit an ordinary trade payment. The goods bypass the intermediary completely, so the intermediary adds nothing that would justify a payment of this size. Pricing is far above market, the intermediary is four months old, and its ownership cannot be established. The activity is outside the customer's declared pattern of EU and Türkiye trade.
narr.explanations: The customer's relationship manager was asked about the commercial rationale. The explanation (a consolidation service) is contradicted by the shipping documents.
narr.actionsOther: Account placed under enhanced monitoring. Relationship review scheduled.
narr.docsText: Four invoices from Gulf Machinery FZE; shipping documents (Pakistan to Belgium); account statement for the period; relationship manager call note.

cases.title: Ferreira: exchange inflows to unused private accounts

timeline.text: Chain analytics confirm indirect mixer exposure. No customer contact, to avoid tipping off.
MLRO decision: report to the FIU.
Report filed with the FIU (own ref STR-2026-0007).

analyst.name: Analyst A
analyst.rationale: Sanctioned-service exposure plus volumes far above declared activity and missing travel-rule data.

mlro.name: MLRO (demo)
mlro.rationale: Reasonable grounds to suspect are met. Report to be filed without delay; pending transactions held until the report is submitted.

narr.legalBasis: AMLR Art. 69(1)(a), or the national law in force until the AMLR applies (10 July 2027)
narr.subjectName: Ms N. Ferreira (fictional; customer ref CUST-11802)
narr.subjectIds: Customer ref CUST-11802; date of birth: placeholder only in this demo
narr.relationship: Retail customer since 2022, freelance designer, standard risk
narr.activitySummary: Four inbound transfers totalling EUR 88,000 from a crypto exchange in Estonia were followed within days by onward transfers of EUR 86,500 to two accounts the customer had not used before.
narr.method: Funds arrive in blocks from the exchange and leave within one to two days to previously unused private accounts. Chain analytics show indirect exposure, two hops back, to a sanctioned mixing service.
narr.expectedActivity: Client invoices of EUR 2,000 to 6,000 a month; crypto trading declared as a side activity with under EUR 5,000 a year.
narr.whyText: Volumes are about twenty times the declared activity. The funds show indirect exposure to a sanctioned service, originator information is missing on three of four inbound transfers, and the money leaves immediately to accounts not used before. No source-of-wealth documents are on file.
narr.explanations: No explanation was sought from the customer, to avoid any risk of tipping off.
narr.docsText: Chain-analytics report; account statement; travel-rule data gap list.

timeline.text: Source of funds documented by notarial deed. Missing item is the senior management approval, a process gap rather than suspicion.
MLRO decision: no report. Approval obtained retroactively and logged as a control finding.

analyst.name: Analyst B
analyst.rationale: Funds and wealth are documented, own-name transfer, no adverse media. The failure is the missing approval.

mlro.name: MLRO (demo)
mlro.rationale: No reasonable grounds to suspect. Process gap raised as an internal finding; approval now on file.
